questions.q: Let $A, B, C$ be three pairwise independent events of a random experiment. If $P\left(\overset{¯}{B} \cup \overset{¯}{C}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}, P\left(A\right) > 0, P\left(B\right) = b$ and $P\left(C\right) = c$, then $P\left(\left(\overset{¯}{B} \cap \overset{¯}{C}\right) A\right) =$
questions.solution:
Given,

$A, B \text{ and } C$ are independent so,

$P\left(A ∩ B\right) = P\left(A\right)P\left(B\right)$

$P\left(B ∩ B\right) = P\left(B\right)P\left(C\right)$

$P\left(C ∩ A\right) = P\left(C\right)P\left(A\right)$

And given $P\left(\overset{¯}{B} ∪ \overset{¯}{C}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Now,

$P\left(\dfrac{\overset{¯}{B} ∩ \overset{¯}{C}}{A}\right) = \dfrac{P\left(\left(\overset{¯}{B} ∩ \overset{¯}{C}\right) ∩ A\right)}{P\left(A\right)}$

By diagram we can see,

$P\left(\left(\overset{¯}{B} ∩ \overset{¯}{C}\right) ∩ A\right) = P\left(A\right) - P\left(A ∩ B\right) - P\left(A ∩ C\right) + P\left(A ∩ B ∩ C\right)$

Also, $P\left(\overset{¯}{B} ∪ \overset{¯}{C}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ 1 - P\left(B ∩ C\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ P\left(B\right)\left(P\left(C\right)\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Rewriting,

$P\left(\left(\overset{¯}{B} ∩ \overset{¯}{C}\right) ∩ A\right) = P\left(A\right) - P\left(A\right)P\left(B\right) - P\left(A\right)P\left(C\right) + P\left(A\right)P\left(B\right)P\left(C\right)$

$⇒ P\left(\left(\overset{¯}{B} ∩ \overset{¯}{C}\right) ∩ A\right) = P\left(A\right)\left[1 - P\left(B\right) - P\left(C\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}\right]$

$⇒ \dfrac{P\left(\left(\overset{¯}{B} ∩ \overset{¯}{C}\right) ∩ A\right)}{P\left(A\right)} = \left[1 - P\left(B\right) - P\left(C\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}\right]$

$⇒ \dfrac{P\left(\left(\overset{¯}{B} ∩ \overset{¯}{C}\right) ∩ A\right)}{P\left(A\right)} = \left(\dfrac{3}{2} - b - C\right)$

So, $P\left(\dfrac{\overset{¯}{B} ∩ \overset{¯}{C}}{A}\right) = \dfrac{3}{2} - b - C$

questions.q: Two dice are thrown and the sum of the numbers appearing on the dice is observed to be a multiple of $4$. If $p$ is the conditional probability that number $4$ has appeared atleast once, then $3p + 2 =$
questions.solution:
Given,

Two dices are thrown so total sample space will be& $36$,

Now let the sum of numbers appearing on dice be a multiple of~$4$~be event& $A$,

So outcomes of event~$A$~will be& $\left\{\left(2, 2\right), \left(1, 3\right), \left(3, 1\right), \left(5, 3\right), \left(3, 5\right), \left(6, 2\right), \left(2, 6\right), \left(4, 4\right), \left(6, 6\right)\right\} \to 9$

So probability will be~$P\left(A\right) = \dfrac{9}{36} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Now let the event~$4$~has already occured be& $B$,

So outcomes will be~$\left\{\left(1, 4\right), \left(4, 1\right), \left(2, 4\right), \left(4, 2\right), \left(3, 4\right), \left(4, 3\right), \left(4, 4\right), \left(4, 5\right), \left(5, 4\right), \left(4, 6\right), \left(6, 4\right)\right\} \to 11$

So probability will be~$P\left(B\right) = \dfrac{11}{36}$

So~$P\left(A ∩ B\right) = \dfrac{1}{36}$

Now~$P\left(B | A\right) = \dfrac{P\left(A ∩ B\right)}{P\left(A\right)} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{36}}{\dfrac{9}{36}} = \dfrac{1}{9}$

So,~$3p + 2 = 3 \times \dfrac{1}{9} + 2 = \dfrac{7}{3}$
